key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer that shapes columnar oxide growth and acts as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: The model links oxide microstructure, oxygen transport, and local tensile stresses to corrosion kinetics and potential crack initiation in zirconium components.
method: Compute ZrOₓ thermochemical and elastic properties using first-principles DFT.
Use molecular dynamics with a DFT-trained machine-learned potential to supply additional model inputs.
Simulate oxide growth in MedeA PhaseField with heterogeneous nucleation, mass transport, interface energies, and strain-dependent phase stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of columnar oxide microstructures and grain-size distributions observed in micrographs, along with an undulating metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors, and the ZrO layer’s contribution to sub-parabolic corrosion kinetics remains a proposed mechanism.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
